title: A Regiment for the Bridge
premise: In the besieged river city of Vellacourt, Elodie Thackeray hides in plain sight as a mapmaker's apprentice, secretly finishing the atlas of the city's bridges and fords that her master, Aldous Vey, supposedly died completing. A stranger arrives bearing letters in Vey's unmistakable hand—proof he lives, and that the atlas contains a military secret the occupying garrison will burn the workshop to possess. As Elodie races to finish the final plate, she discovers Vey encoded the true crossing routes into the maps and sold them to the enemy, making her the only living person who can either expose or protect his betrayal. In the end she completes the atlas, chooses truth over loyalty to her dead master, and delivers it to the city's defenders as the bridge burns behind her.
about_author: Dominic Crane is a former surveyor's assistant who spent a decade restoring antique maps before turning to historical fiction. His novels are known for their obsessive cartographic detail and quiet, stubborn protagonists who outlast empires.

chapters.title: The Ink That Outlives
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In the occupied workshop, she inks plates of the dead master's atlas by candlelight, hiding her competence behind a plodding apprentice manner. The garrison requisitions paper, and the emotional beat is the loneliness of guarding a secret no one left alive shares. Ends with her touching Vey's unfinished marginal note: 'finish the river.'

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A scarred traveler named Corvin arrives asking for 'the hand of Aldous Vey,' producing letters written in the master's living hand. Elodie denies everything, heart pounding, but Corvin leaves a letter behind addressed to her by name. The beat is fear curdling into betrayal: her invisibility was an illusion.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, with an interlude in Corvin's. She studies Vey's letters and realizes the atlas's bridge surveys contain corrected fords—knowledge worth a battle. Corvin claims he was Vey's courier and wants the finished atlas for the resistance. Elodie must decide whether to trust a stranger or the dead. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Garrison's Cartographer
chapters.summary: Introducing Captain Rennard, the occupation's own mapmaker, who requisitions the workshop and begins copying Vey's plates. Elodie's POV as she watches her master's work being turned to the occupier's purposes. She plants deliberate errors in the copies. Beat: first act of quiet defiance, and the first taste of power's danger.

chapters.title: Letters from a Drowned Man
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. He confesses Vey is alive—hiding in the marshes—but that Vey sold the crossing routes to the garrison before defecting, and the atlas is both his ransom and his confession. Corvin wants it finished to prove Vey's guilt to the resistance. Elodie's loyalty to her master cracks. Beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: The Final Plate
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Working under Rennard's increasingly suspicious eye, she completes the last map of the great bridge, discovering Vey's encoded confession hidden in the soundings. Rennard finds her working after curfew and offers her protection in exchange for the original. Beat: temptation—the safety she always wanted, at the price of truth.

chapters.title: Ash on the Vellum
chapters.summary: Elodie and Corvin's POV alternating. Rennard discovers the falsified copies and orders the workshop searched; Elodie smuggles the original atlas out in a map chest while the garrison burns Vey's correspondence. Her fellow apprentice Tomas is taken for questioning. Beat: the price of survival becomes a bill others pay.

chapters.title: The Marshes of Vey
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She finds Vey alive in the marshes, old, cowardly, and unrepentant: he sold the crossings to buy his life and expects her gratitude for the trade that kept her safe too. She confronts him with his own encoded confession. Beat: the death of loyalty; she leaves him his letters and takes the truth.

chapters.title: The Burning Bridge
chapters.summary: Elodie and Corvin deliver the atlas to the city's defenders as the garrison moves to seize the bridge. Climax: the resistance uses the true fords to ambush the crossing while Rennard, realizing the copies were false, marches his men onto the bridge as it is fired. Beat: truth made flesh in gunpowder and flame.

chapters.title: A New Hand
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, weeks later. The city holds; Rennard is dead or fled; Vey's name is disgraced and Tomas freed. Offered a place as the city's official cartographer, Elodie signs the new atlas with her own name for the first time. Beat: resolution—survival was never hiding; it was deciding what was worth being seen for.
